title: Hardwood Floor Installation in Lynnwood: 5 Questions to Ask Before You Sign
meta: Before signing a Lynnwood hardwood installation contract, ask what labor covers, what is under your floor, the method, who does the work and the timeline. Wills Flooring explains.

blocks.lead: Before you sign a hardwood installation contract in Lynnwood, get written answers to five questions: what the labor price includes, what is under your current floor, which installation method and subfloor prep is planned, who actually does the work and backs it, and what the schedule expects from you.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring publishes its labor rates so you can check the first answer before we arrive: $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid, $2.75 for unfinished, $125 per stair, 500 sq ft minimum. Material and prep are quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.html: Our showroom sits on 196th St SW, so a lot of Lynnwood homeowners walk in with a competing quote in hand and ask us to read it. The common problem is not the price. It is that the quote does not say what the price covers, what the installer expects to find under the carpet in a 1970s Alderwood split-level, or who will be on site. These five questions fix that. Ask them of anyone, including us, and put the answers in the contract before you sign for a hardwood floor installation.

blocks.note: A quote that gives one lump sum with none of these lines is not a quote you can compare with anyone else's. Our price list is public so the labor line is never a mystery.

blocks.text: Question 2: What is under my current floor, and does it change the plan?

items.title: Oak under the carpet
items.text: Most 1960s Lynnwood ramblers in Alderwood and Meadowdale have original oak strip under the carpet. If it is sound, refinishing it at $3.99 per sq ft all-in beats installing new wood. Any estimator who does not lift a carpet corner before quoting new hardwood is skipping a step.

items.title: Particleboard underlayment
items.text: Many 1970s and 80s split-levels have particleboard over the plywood subfloor. Nails do not hold in it and it swells with moisture. It has to come out before a nail-down floor, and that removal must be a line on the quote.

items.title: Slab on the lower level
items.text: Split-level and daylight-basement lower floors are concrete. Solid hardwood nailed down is off the table there; the answer is engineered plank, glued or floated over a moisture barrier, after a moisture test.

items.title: Old sheet vinyl or tile
items.text: Vinyl and adhesive from before the mid-1980s can contain asbestos. It should be tested, and if positive, encapsulated under new underlayment rather than sanded or scraped. Ask how the installer handles this before anyone starts tearing up the kitchen.

blocks.text: Question 3: Which installation method, and what does my subfloor need first?

a.title: The right answer when
items: The subfloor is plywood or OSB over joists, typical of Lynnwood ramblers and upper floors
You are installing 3/4 in solid or thicker engineered boards
The floor is flat to within 3/16 in over 10 ft, or will be after prep
You want the quietest, most solid-feeling floor

b.title: The right answer when
items: The subfloor is a concrete slab, as on split-level lower floors
You chose engineered plank with a click or tongue-and-groove edge
There is radiant heat, which nails would puncture
A townhome HOA requires a sound-rated underlayment

blocks.title: Get the flatness and moisture numbers in writing:
blocks.text: Ask the installer what flatness tolerance they work to and what moisture reading they need in the subfloor and the wood before installing. If the answer is a shrug, that is your answer. We put a straightedge and a moisture meter on every Lynnwood floor at the free estimate and write the readings on the quote.
Questions 4 and 5: who does the work, and what happens when

items.text: Ask for the contractor license number, proof of insurance, and whether the crew are employees or a sub hired for the day. Ask what the workmanship warranty covers and for how long. Wills Flooring has been licensed and insured since 2013 and backs every installation with a 1-year workmanship warranty.
items.note: For unfinished floors, ask who sands and finishes; we are Bona Certified Craftsmen and do it ourselves

items.d: Question 5, part one: before the crew
items.text: When does the wood arrive, how long does it acclimate in the house, and what do you need to clear? Solid hardwood usually sits three to five days in the rooms where it goes. Furniture, rugs and anything on the floor should be out before delivery.
items.note: Ask whether the thermostat needs to be at living temperature during acclimation; it does

items.d: Question 5, part two: the install days
items.text: A 1,000 sq ft prefinished engineered floor in a Martha Lake rambler is typically two to three days of installation. Unfinished floors add sanding and three coats of finish, which adds three to four days and a cure period before furniture.
items.note: 1,000 × $3.25 = $3,250 labor for prefinished; 1,000 × $2.75 + 1,000 × $3.99 = $6,740 for unfinished plus site finishing

items.text: Ask who reinstalls baseboards, who removes the debris, and when you can walk on it and move furniture back. Get the walkthrough and final payment tied to your sign-off, not the crew's departure.
items.note: Prefinished floors: walk on immediately, furniture same day with felt pads

blocks.text: Answers that should make you walk away

items.html: One lump-sum number with no breakdown. You cannot tell what is included, and every surprise becomes a change order.
"We'll deal with the subfloor when we open it up." That is a blank check. The estimate should include a look under the carpet and a written allowance for likely prep.
No license number on the quote. Washington requires one, and it takes thirty seconds to check online.
A deposit over half the job. Material deposits are normal. Most of the labor should be paid when the floor is done and you have walked it.
"Acclimation is not necessary." It is, especially for solid wood in a damp Snohomish County winter. Skipping it is how gaps and cupping appear the following summer.
Quoting new hardwood without checking for the old. In Lynnwood, that is leaving a refinishable oak floor, and thousands of dollars, under the carpet.
Every line itemized: labor, material, underlayment, removal, prep, stairs, trim, furniture.
A written note of what is under the current floor and what the estimator saw when they lifted a corner.
Flatness and moisture readings and the installation method that follows from them.
License, insurance and the warranty terms on the paperwork, not just in conversation.
Delivery, acclimation, install and walkthrough dates plus a list of what you need to do before each one.
Samples seen in your own light. A mobile showroom visit puts the boards on your Lynnwood floor next to your cabinets, which is the only place a color decision should be made.

faq.q: How much does hardwood floor installation cost in Lynnwood?
faq.a: Wills Flooring charges $3.25 per sq ft of labor for engineered or solid hardwood and $2.75 for unfinished boards, with a 500 sq ft minimum and $125 per stair. Material, underlayment, old-floor removal and subfloor prep are quoted separately at the free in-home estimate.

faq.q: Should I check for hardwood under my carpet before buying new flooring?
faq.a: Yes, always. Most Lynnwood homes built before 1975 have oak strip under the carpet. If it is sound, sanding and refinishing it costs $3.99 per sq ft all-in, less than a new floor, and keeps the original character. We lift a corner at every estimate.

faq.q: Does hardwood need to acclimate before installation?
faq.a: Solid hardwood does, usually three to five days inside the rooms where it will be installed, with the house at normal living temperature. Many engineered products need less, but we still check the moisture of the wood and the subfloor before starting.

faq.q: Can hardwood be installed on the lower level of a split-level home?
faq.a: On a concrete slab, yes, but only engineered plank, glued down or floated over a moisture barrier, after the slab tests dry. Solid hardwood nailed down is not an option over concrete. Many Lynnwood split-levels end up with solid upstairs and engineered downstairs in a matching color.

faq.q: How long does a hardwood installation take?
faq.a: A 1,000 sq ft prefinished floor typically takes two to three days after acclimation. Unfinished floors add sanding and three coats of finish, roughly three to four more days plus cure time. Removal and subfloor prep add time, which we schedule up front.

faq.q: What should a hardwood installation contract include?
faq.a: Itemized labor, material and prep lines, the installation method, the flatness and moisture readings from the estimate, the license number, insurance, warranty terms, a payment schedule and dates for delivery, acclimation, installation and walkthrough. Wills Flooring writes all of that on the quote at the estimate.
